body: Duquesne Capital 1981-2010: ~30% average annual return, widely reported as no losing year, though some reports say 2010 (closing year) was down ~5%; returns never publicly audited, so treat as press-reported. Lead PM of Soros's Quantum Fund 1988-2000. Structural edge: in the Soros seat he could deploy multi-billion positions in currencies, bonds and stocks with leverage. Process edge: markets are driven by liquidity (central banks, credit), not earnings; he looks 18-24 months ahead; he sizes very large when conviction and risk/reward line up and cuts fast when wrong ('it's not whether you're right or wrong, but how much you make when right'). Signature trade: Sept 1992 short of sterling before ERM exit (~$1bn, Wikipedia puts Quantum gain at ~$1.8bn for the week). Biggest mistake: 1999-2000 he shorted tech, gave up, then bought ~$6bn of tech near the March 2000 top (unverified figure) and Quantum lost heavily; he left in April 2000. He also says he sold Nvidia too early in 2024. Copyable for an individual: track RBI/Fed liquidity and credit spreads as the master variable; make few large bets, not many small ones; exit as soon as the thesis breaks; when a regime changes, change your mind without ego. Not copyable: leverage, FX/bond access, information flow.

data.copyable: liquidity dashboard, concentration with stop discipline
data.edge_process: liquidity first, 18-24m horizon, concentrated sizing, fast cuts
data.edge_structural: multi-asset leverage, scale, macro information network
data.mistakes: bought tech at 2000 top; sold Nvidia early (2024)

title: Stanley Druckenmiller - liquidity-driven macro, concentrated sizing
